Why the PBM Database

One therapy, many names in the literature.

Published studies do not always use the same name for photobiomodulation. The database brings this varied literature together.

Examples of terms and descriptions in papers

Low-level light therapyLow-level laser therapyLow-power laser therapyLow-intensity laser therapyCold laser therapy (CLT)Laser acupunctureLaser treatmentLaser light irradiationLED phototherapyLight-emitting diode irradiationRed-light photostimulationPhotobiomodulationPhotobiostimulationPhotostimulationNear-infrared light treatmentFar-red lightHelium–neon laser irradiationTranscranial laser stimulation660 nm LED light source904 nm laser

Some phrases describe the light source or wavelength rather than a standardized synonym.

How the database was built

Search terms, citation checks and manual review

The database was compiled by searching for PBM research under a range of terms and reviewing candidate records. Forward citation searches—checking papers that cite relevant studies already found—help identify additional papers. Manual review excludes unrelated keyword matches, such as “red light” papers about traffic signals.

Organized records

PBM Database

  • Study models, methods and publication details
  • Wavelengths, light delivery and treatment parameters
  • Annotations flag comparisons, cautions and notable findings
  • Direct links to original research papers

Structured markings can make key details quicker to locate than screening PubMed records one by one.

Open the database  →

The PBM Database is a manually curated resource that continues to be updated; it is not a formal systematic review.

Database annotations

What the database symbols mean

The symbols make key details—study models and methods, light delivery and findings—easier to scan. The number beside each marking shows how many database records carry it; records can have several markings, so counts overlap. Curator highlights and interpretive notes reflect the curator’s reading, not an independent rating of study quality.
